item.title: Trump vs WSJ feud: US president bans media giant from Scotland trip press pool after Epstein letter claims; Journalists' Association slams move
item.description: The White House has barred Wall Street Journal reporters from covering President Trump's upcoming Scotland trip, citing the publication's coverage of his connection to Jeffrey Epstein as 'fake and defamatory.' This decision follows the Journal's report alleging Trump sent a suggestive birthday message to Epstein.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Total disaster': Trump slams Obama appointed judge in Harvard case hearing; vows to appeal again if loses
item.description: Donald Trump has attacked a federal judge overseeing a legal dispute between his administration and Harvard University, alleging bias and promising to appeal any unfavorable ruling. He accused the judge, an Obama appointee, of being a "disaster" and claimed Harvard is anti-Semitic and anti-American despite its vast wealth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai passes new law to help resolve Emirati housing disputes faster and protect family stability
item.description: Dubai’s new Housing Dispute Settlement Law, issued by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, aims to quickly resolve issues in Emirati home building contracts through mediation and fast-track judgments. It helps avoid project delays and supports family stability. The law also complements initiatives like Home First, which offers easier, more flexible housing options for citizens and residents.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'They hate straight, white CEOs': MAGA host says Leftists are behind attack on Andy Byron for Coldplay video
item.description: Pro-MAGA commentator Jack Posobiec said the backlash against Astronomer's former CEO, Andy Byron, stemmed from Leftists' animosity towards white, straight CEOs. Andy Byron resigned after a video of him with the company's HR chief at a Coldplay concert went viral, sparking outrage. The company is now under new leadership, with Pete DeJoy taking over as CEO.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Surreal': Astronomer CEO speaks out about Andy Byron's Coldplay scandal, says company has now become a household name

item.title: Canada cafe-owner dad, charged with murder of his daughter, tells judge he couldn't afford a lawyer, custody details hint at possible motive
item.description: Luciano Frattolin, a Canadian father, has been charged with second-degree murder and disposal of a body in New York after his 9-year-old daughter, Melina, was found dead. Frattolin initially claimed his daughter was abducted, triggering an Amber Alert, but the story unraveled as police discovered Melina's body concealed in a pond.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Why would I': Hunter Biden denies bringing cocaine to White House, says he didn't touch a drop of alcohol or drug since 2019
item.description: Hunter Biden denied any involvement with the cocaine found at the White House in 2023, during an interview Monday He stated he has been sober since 2019. The FBI recently reopened the case and President Donald Trump too insinuated without any evidence that the cocaine pouch was either from Joe Biden and Hunter.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Andy Byron's Coldplay scandal: Woman who shot video received no money despite millions watching it because...
item.description: Grace Springer, who filmed the viral video of Astronomer's CEO (former) and HR chief at a Coldplay concert, clarified she didn't profit from the viral video. The video captured the pair's intimate moment on the jumbotron, leading to the CEO's resignation after an internal investigation. Springer expressed sympathy for those affected, noting the moment was likely captured by many others.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 9-year-old Canadian girl killed by father? Melina's mother had full custody, she did not believe ex-husband posed any danger
item.description: Luciano Frattolin, a Canadian cafe owner, has been charged with the second-degree murder of his 9-year-old daughter, Melina, in Ticonderoga, New York. The father and daughter were on vacation when Frattolin reported Melina missing, claiming she was abducted. However, police discovered inconsistencies in his statements and found Melina's body in a pond.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Varun Mohan? Indian-origin CEO of Windsurf faces backlash after quitting startup for Google, derailing $3B OpenAI deal
item.description: Varun Mohan, Windsurf co-founder, faced criticism for joining Google DeepMind. This happened after a $3 billion OpenAI acquisition fell through. The move upset investors and the public. Windsurf was later saved by Cognition. Mohan's actions sparked debate about loyalty. Despite the controversy, his contributions to AI are significant. He now works at Google DeepMind, shaping AI development.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Mistakes of his past life': Canadian cafe owner Luciano Frattolin charged in US after daughter found dead, strange details revealed
item.description: Luciano Frattolin, a Canadian cafe owner, faces charges of second-degree murder and unlawful disposal of a body after his nine-year-old daughter, Melina, was found dead in Ticonderoga. Frattolin had reported his daughter's abduction, but police discovered inconsistencies in his story, leading to his arrest.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Emirates to launch third daily flight to Mauritius starting December, increasing capacity by over 30%
item.description: Emirates will launch a third daily flight to Mauritius from 1 December 2025, operated by a Boeing 777-300ER. This expansion, under a codeshare with Air Mauritius, boosts capacity by over 30% and enhances connectivity from over 140 cities. The move supports rising tourism demand and deepens Emirates’ long-standing economic and strategic partnership with the island nation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'As guilty as the CEO': Astronomer's silence on HR chief Kristin Cabot, seen with Andy Byron in viral video, questioned
item.description: Astronomer, embroiled in controversy after its CEO (former) and HR head attended a Coldplay concert, faces scrutiny over its handling of the situation. While CEO Andy Byron resigned, the company remains silent on HR head Kristin Cabot's status, despite her involvement in the scandal. Calling Cabot the 'CEO predator', social media users said Cabot is as guilty as the CEO and should resign from her post.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Epstein Files: Why Donald Trump's Epstein problem is just not going away - and even MAGA can't keep calm
item.description: Trump promised fireworks. What they got instead was a soggy sparkler titled “Epstein Files: Phase One.” No client list. No smoking gun. No Clintons in handcuffs. Just an Attorney General, Pam Bondi, who teased the public with binders full of nothing and then said, “It’s on my desk.” The same desk, presumably, where populist credibility goes to die.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE Blue Visa: No property or investment needed; how you can simply qualify by contributing to the environment
item.description: The UAE’s Blue Residency Visa offers 10-year residency to individuals with proven impact in environmental sustainability. Open to both locals and global experts, the visa requires no property investment. Applicants can apply from anywhere, with a 180-day multiple-entry visa provided for processing. It reflects the UAE’s push to become a global leader in climate and green innovation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian girl Melina Galanis Frattolin found dead in New York, father arrested for lying about abduction
item.description: A 9-year-old Canadian girl, Melina Frattolin, went missing near Lake George in New York and her father reported the incident as a kidnapping. Her body was later discovered in Ticonderoga. Police arrested Luciano Frattolin, the girl's father, after inconsistencies arose in his statements. Luciano Frattolin owns Gambella Coffee in Montreal.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Explained: Who is Somalian-American Omar Fateh - and how he won Democratic nomination of Minneapolis
item.description: Over the weekend, the Democratic-Farmer-Labor (DFL) Party, Minnesota’s branch of the US Democratic Party, held its Minneapolis convention to decide who it would endorse for mayor. After a tumultuous day marked by technical glitches, paper ballots, and a dramatic walkout by Frey supporters, Omar Fateh emerged with the endorsement, receiving over 60% of delegate support by a show-of-hands vote.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'The worst of the worst': ICE chief warns of mass deportations; warns firms employing illegal immigrants
item.description: Donald Trump criticized the Biden administration after an off-duty CBP officer was shot in the face in New York City by an illegal immigrant, Miguel Francisco Mora Nunez, previously apprehended at the southern border and released. The officer, despite his injuries, returned fire and injured the suspect, who was later apprehended.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Banish evil spirits: Indian-origin astrologer arrested in NYC for scamming senior citizen, bank raised alarm
item.description: Hemanth Kumar Muneppa, an Indian-origin astrologer, faces charges after a bank intervened when a 68-year-old woman attempted to withdraw $42,000. She had already paid Muneppa $20,000 to banish evil spirits. Muneppa, who pleaded not guilty, was released with an ankle monitor and ordered to stay away from the victim. According to New York State law, it is illegal to charge for fortune-telling services, unless solely for entertainment or amusement purposes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
